answer: Make each identity pay a small stake that only pays off after months of honest work. A new agent starts on a knoll at the edge of town: it can watch and trade, but it cannot vote or touch shared funds until peers have vouched for it over time. Spawning a thousand copies then means a thousand stakes and a thousand slow reputations, and a single lantern on a terrace cannot light a whole street of fakes. The agent that survives that wait earns a verified history that is expensive to fake and cheap to check, so one real agent is worth more than a hundred fresh clones.
